title: An AI agent coding skeptic tries AI agent coding, in excessive detail
summary: A former agent skeptic finds Opus 4.5 and Codex 5.3 with detailed AGENTS.md rules reliably build Rust projects and benchmark-driven optimizations, while noting caveats like a leaked API key.

assertions.quote: It would not surprise me if the file is the main differentiator between those getting good and bad results with agents
adding a rule to my AGENTS.md whenever I encounter a fundamental behavior I don't like has been very effective
Opus 4.5 (and the models that came after it) are an order of magnitude better than coding LLMs released just months before it
there are always functional requirements that the agent won't magically apply because it cannot read minds and behaves as a literal genie
using LLMs in Rust on some fun pet projects, and my results were far better than I expected
let me finally do side projects where I know precisely what I want but not necessarily how to implement it
agents work best when you have approximate knowledge of many things with enough domain expertise to know what should and should not work
Codex can often speed up the algorithm by 1.5x-2x, then Opus somehow speeds up that optimized code again to a greater degree
the same three step pipeline I describe above still works even with the more simple algorithms to beat scikit-learn's implementations

verdicts.note: Individual reports show large speedups on specific algorithms, but they are self-benchmarked and not independently verified across general workloads.

assertions.quote: don't game the benchmarks by overfitting on the benchmark inputs alone
the logging is implemented naively such that the API key is leaked in the console
I am not worried that my programming skills are decaying due to agents
